title: Protocol Considerations for In Vitro Metabolic Glycoengineering of Non-Natural Glycans
protocol: Incubate cells with sugar analogs Ac4ManNAz.
Incubate cells with sugar analogs Ac4ManNAl.
Incubate cells with sugar analogs Ac4ManLev.
Incubate cells with sugar analogs Ac5ManNTGc.
Use ManNAc as a control for increased flux through the sialic acid pathway.
Use Ac4ManNAc to control for increased flux and off-target responses from SCFA protecting groups.
Label sterile 24-well tissue culture plates with the desired concentrations of SCFA-derivatized analogs or higher millimolar concentrations of free hydroxyl analogs.
Set up triplicate wells for each concentration.
Add the appropriate volume of 10 mM analog stock solution to give the desired final concentration after adding 0.5 ml of cells.
For volumes less than 1-2 μl, use 10× volumes of a 1 mM stock solution to avoid pipetting errors.
Leave plates in a sterile tissue culture hood with lids open for approximately 15 minutes to allow ethanol to evaporate.
Harvest Jurkat cells as described or use usual methods for alternate cell lines while ethanol is evaporating.
Adjust Jurkat cell density to 5 × 10^5 cells/ml in complete RPMI-1640 for a 48-hour experiment.
Mix thoroughly to obtain a homogeneous single-cell suspension.
For a 72-hour experiment, adjust the cell density to 2.5 × 10^5 cells/ml.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 48 or 72 hours after adding 0.5 ml of cell suspension to each well.
Mix cell culture thoroughly by gently pipetting up and down several times with a 1-ml pipette.
Count an aliquot of the mixed cell culture to determine cell density.
Use the cells for toxicity, labeling, or functional assays.
Use the minimal amount of trypsin and shortest exposure time needed to detach adherent cells for flow cytometry analysis.
Monitor metabolic incorporation of MGE analogs into adherent cells by fluorescence microscopy.
Monitor metabolic incorporation of MGE analogs into adherent cells using a microplate reader assay.
Study the incorporation of analogs as a function of time.
Prepare separate plates for each specified time point if short intervals are used.
Increase initial cell density to 1 × 10^6 cells/ml for time points less than 24 hours.
For multi-day time points, prepare larger-volume cultures at an initial volume of 1 ml.
Remove 0.5 ml from the culture each day for analysis.
Replenish removed volume with 0.5 ml fresh medium.
Maintain initial analog concentration by adding appropriate volumes of analog to the replenished medium.
Add ethanol to maintain consistent solvent concentration in each well if analog is directly added to the culture.
Follow routine methods to maintain Jurkat cells, a lymphocyte line derived from human acute T cell leukemia (clone E6-1).
Add Jurkat cells to complete RPMI-1640 to attain a cell density of ∼1–2.5 × 10^5 cells/ml.
Transfer the cell mixture to a tissue culture flask or dish.
Place the tissue culture flask or dish in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Incubate for up to 4 days to allow cells to reach a density of ∼2 × 10^6 cells/ml.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15- or 50-ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 3.5 min at 1300 × g, room temperature.
Carefully discard the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells in 10 ml of prewarmed (37°C) complete RPMI-1640.
Disperse cell clumps by gently pipetting up and down several times.
Count cells using an electronic cell counter or hemacytometer.
Replate an aliquot of cells as described.
Place the stock flask in the incubator.
Use the remaining harvested cells for MGE protocols.
Incubate cells with SCFA-monosaccharide analogs to assess cytotoxicity.
Evaluate cell viability using Basic Protocol 1.
Identify analogs that inhibit cell growth.
Quantify inhibition as an IC50 value.
Conduct short-term exposure experiments for 2, 3, or 5 days.
Assess actual cell death over concentration ranges used in MGE experiments.
Use trypan blue to detect dead cells if fewer cells than negative controls are present.
Run standard apoptosis assays to determine programmed cell death induction.
Evaluate metabolic state of the cells using the MTT assay.
Monitor cell counts over a 2-week period to determine lethality.
Use IC50 data obtained from 2-, 3-, or 5-day cell counts for determining safe analog levels.
Obtain LD50 data from 15-day experiments to determine safe analog levels.
Incubate Jurkat cells (1 × 10^5 cells in 0.5 ml) with analog (e.g., 2 at 0-320 µM) in a 24-well plate for 3 days in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Gently pipette Jurkat cells up and down using a 1-ml pipette to dislodge cell clumps on day 3.
Transfer two 100-µl aliquots of cells to 10 ml PBS in cuvettes on day 3.
Measure and record the cell density using a cell counter or hemacytometer on day 3.
Add 1 ml medium to each well after measuring cell density on day 3.
Gently pipette Jurkat cells up and down using a 1-ml pipette to dislodge cell clumps on day 5.
Transfer two 100-µl aliquots of cells to 10 ml PBS in cuvettes on day 5.
Measure and record the cell density using a cell counter or hemacytometer on day 5.
Add 1 ml medium to each well after measuring cell density on day 5.
Gently pipette Jurkat cells up and down using a 1-ml pipette to dislodge clumps on days 7, 9, 11, and 13.
Remove 1 ml suspension from each well and add 1 ml fresh medium on days 7, 9, 11, and 13.
Gently pipette Jurkat cells up and down using a 1-ml pipette to dislodge clumps on day 15.
Take a 1-ml aliquot of cells and add it to 10 ml PBS in a cuvette on day 15.
Measure and record the cell density using a cell counter or hemacytometer on day 15.
Calculate the relative cell number for each analog concentration with respect to the ethanol control for days 3, 5, and 15.

Plot relative cell number with respect to analog concentration for days 2 or 3, 5, and 15 to determine the IC50 or LD50 value (concentrations where relative cell numbers are 50% of untreated controls).
Quantify non-natural glycan display on the cell surface as described in Basic Protocol 4.
Measure total and glycoconjugate-bound sialic acids using the periodate-resorcinol assay.
Incubate Jurkat cells or other line being tested with sugar analogs as described, using 25-cm² tissue culture flasks instead of 24-well plates and seeding approximately 1 × 10⁷ cells in 10 ml.
Use a high-flux, low-toxicity analog such as compound 6 in all experiments as a positive control.
Harvest Jurkat cells by gently pipetting up and down using a 1-ml pipet to dislodge clumps and transferring to a 15-ml centrifuge tube.
Detach adherent cells from the culture flask using trypsin and transfer to a 15-ml tube.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 1000 × g, room temperature.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 10 ml PBS by gentle pipetting.
Centrifuge cells for 3.5 min at 1300 × g, room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 5 ml PBS by gentle pipetting.
Repeat washing two more times to thoroughly remove FBS from the cells.
Remove two 100-µl aliquots of cells and determine density using a cell counter or hemacytometer.
Add PBS to each sample to obtain a density of 1 × 10^6 cells/ml, pipetting gently to ensure homogeneity.
Aliquot 1 ml suspension to three 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes containing 1 × 10^6 cells per tube.
Pellet cells by centrifuging for 3.5 min at 1300 × g, room temperature.
Resuspend cells in 300 μl PBS.
Freeze tubes in a –80°C freezer for approximately 1 hour or on pulverized dry ice for 5-10 minutes.
Thaw tubes in a 37°C water bath.
Repeat the freeze-thaw cycle for a total of three cycles.
Remove 0.4 M periodic acid and 6% (w/v) resorcinol from freezer and thaw at room temperature.
Warm t-butyl alcohol to 25°C.
Prewarm heating block to 100°C.
Prepare a fresh 1 mM sialic acid solution by diluting the 10 mM stock in PBS.
Use the 1 mM solution to prepare 300-μl standards of 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 μM as follows:
Add 3 μl sialic acid to 297 μl PBS for a concentration of 10 μM.
Add 6 μl sialic acid to 294 μl PBS for a concentration of 20 μM.
Add 9 μl sialic acid to 291 μl PBS for a concentration of 30 μM.
Add 12 μl sialic acid to 288 μl PBS for a concentration of 40 μM.
Add 15 μl sialic acid to 285 μl PBS for a concentration of 50 μM.
Add 5 µl of 0.4 M periodic acid to each sample and standard.
Vortex the samples and place on ice for 15 min.
Incubate samples for 80 min at 37°C.
Prepare resorcinol working reagent by mixing 1.5 ml 6% resorcinol, 1.5 ml 2.5 mM CuSO4, 6.6 ml deionized H2O, and 5.4 ml concentrated HCl.
Add 500 µl of the resorcinol working reagent to each tube, vortex, and incubate for 10 min in a water-filled heating block at 100°C.
Remove tubes from the heating block and cool rapidly in room temperature water.
Add 500 µl t-butyl alcohol to each tube and mix by vortexing.
Centrifuge samples for 2 min at maximum speed in a benchtop microcentrifuge.
Aliquot samples into 96-well plates (two wells per sample).
Measure absorbance of the samples at 630 nm.
Aliquot precisely the same volume into each well for spectroscopic readings.
Measure absorbance using a microplate reader to allow for smaller volumes and higher throughput.
Adjust sample volume in wells if necessary for accurate spectroscopic readings.
Introduce tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) as a mild reducing agent before chemoselective ligation of thiols.
Perform chemoselective ligation of thiols after reduction with TCEP.
Incubate Jurkat cells with the appropriate test analog.
Incubate Jurkat cells with the control as described in Basic Protocol 1.
Seed approximately 1 × 10^6 cells in 2 ml of medium per sample for incubation.
Prepare a sufficient number of cells at the end of 2-3 days to perform quantitative estimation in triplicate.
Use as few as 2 × 10^5 cells per replicate if cell availability is limited.
Maintain Jurkat cell density between 0.5 × 10^6 and 2 × 10^6 cells/ml during incubation.
Gently pipette cell suspension up and down using a 5-ml pipet to dislodge clumps.
Count an aliquot of the cell suspension to determine cell density.
Centrifuge cells in 15-ml tubes for 3.5 min at 1300 × g, room temperature, and discard supernatant.
Add 3 ml PBS and resuspend cells by gentle pipetting.
Aliquot 1 ml resuspended cells to three 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes (maximum of 2 × 10^6 cells/tube).
Wash cells twice with freshly prepared biotin buffer, then twice with PBS.
Centrifuge cells 2.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature, discard the supernatant, and gently resuspend in a volume of 1 ml for each wash.
Centrifuge cells 3.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature, and resuspend gently in 250 μl biotin buffer.
Add 250 µl of 5 mM biotin hydrazide and mix immediately by gentle pipetting.
Lay tubes flat on the benchtop at room temperature for 2 hr, mixing by gentle inversion every 15 min.
Proceed to step 12.
Wash cells as in step 6a.
Centrifuge cells 3.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature, and resuspend gently in 250 µl CuAAC buffer.
Add 250 µl of 1 mM biotin alkyne and mix immediately by gentle pipetting.
Lay tubes flat on the benchtop at room temperature for 2 hr, mixing by gentle inversion every 15 min.
Proceed to step 12.
Wash cells as in step 6a.
Dilute 5 µl of 4 mM biotin-PEG4-DBCO in 495 µl PBS.
Centrifuge cells 3.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature, and resuspend gently in 500 µl diluted biotin-PEG4-DBCO.
Lay tubes flat on the benchtop at room temperature for 1 hr, mixing by gentle inversion every 15 min.
Proceed to step 12.
Wash cells as in step 6a.
Centrifuge cells 3.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature, and resuspend gently in 250 µl CuAAC buffer.
Add 250 µl of 1 mM biotin azide and mix immediately by gentle pipetting.
Lay tubes flat on the benchtop at room temperature for 2 hr, mixing by gentle inversion every 15 min.
Proceed to step 12.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Centrifuge cells for 3.5 min at 3000 × g at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend cells in 1 ml of PBS.
Prepare a 10 mM solution of TCEP by adding 2.87 mg to 1 ml of PBS.
Centrifuge cells for 3.5 min at 3000 × g at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend cells in 360 µl of PBS.
Add 40 µl of 10 mM TCEP to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM.
Lay tubes flat on the benchtop at room temperature for 1 hour.
Mix by gentle inversion every 15 minutes.
Prepare a fresh 5 mM MB solution by adding 3.9 mg EZ-Link maleimide PEG2-biotin to 1.5 ml PBS.
Add 100 µl of the prepared solution to each sample and mix immediately by gentle pipetting.
Lay tubes flat on the benchtop at room temperature for 1 hr, mixing by gentle inversion every 15 min.
Cool 50 ml ASB and 50 ml PBS in an ice bath while cells are labeling.
Centrifuge labeled samples 3.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 ml ice-cold ASB.
Repeat wash two more times, but resuspend the third pellet in 100 µl ASB.
Dilute 2.8 mg/ml FITC-avidin 1:250 in PBS and mix well, keeping it in the dark on ice for no more than 12 hr.
Add 100 µl diluted FITC-avidin to each tube (final 5.6 µg/ml), mix immediately by gentle pipetting, and incubate on ice out of direct light for 15 min.
Centrifuge FITC-labeled cells 3.5 min at 3000 × g, room temperature.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells gently in 100 µl ASB.
Repeat FITC-avidin incubation as previously done.
React cells with FITC-avidin twice to remove any remaining free biotin reagents.
Collect untreated Jurkat cells and add approximately 1 × 10^6 cells to each of two 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes.
Wash the collected cells twice, resuspend in 500 µl PBS, and transfer to 5-ml polystyrene tubes.
Keep the samples on ice out of direct light for adjusting flow cytometer settings and defining healthy cell population.
Centrifuge labeled samples for 3.5 minutes at 3000 × g at room temperature.
Discard supernatant after centrifugation and resuspend cells gently in 1 ml ice-cold ASB.
Repeat the wash two more times, but resuspend the third pellet in 500 µl PBS and transfer to 5-ml polystyrene tubes.
Keep samples on ice out of direct light for up to 3 hours before analysis by flow cytometry.
Analyze samples by flow cytometry, collecting at least 10,000 events for each run.
Run analysis twice for each sample to ensure accurate results.
Measure the relative fluorescence content of cells using the geometric mean in arbitrary units.
